title: High-precision CRISPR-Cas12a-based SNV detection on synthetic DNA and liquid biopsies
author: Kohabir, Linthorst, et al.
materials: Q5 Hot Start High-Fidelity DNA Polymerase
Low volume 384-well black flat bottom polystyrene NBS microplate

steps.title: Seed cells in culture flask
steps.instruction: Seed approximately 3 × 10⁶ cells in appropriate growth medium in a T175 flask or a 15 cm dish.

steps.title: Incubate cells for one week
steps.instruction: Place the flask/dish in a stationary incubator set to 37 °C with 5 % CO₂ and grow the cells for about 1 week without changing the medium.

steps.title: Harvest conditioned medium
steps.instruction: Collect the conditioned medium, centrifuge, optionally filter, and store at –20 °C.

substeps.instruction: Collect the conditioned medium into a Falcon tube suitable for centrifugation.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube and discard the pellet.
Optional: filter the supernatant through a 0.45 µm sterile filter.
Store the processed medium at –20 °C until further use.

steps.title: Copy fluorescence data to analysis software
steps.instruction: Copy the raw fluorescence columns from the Excel file into the chosen analysis software.

steps.title: Import data into GraphPad Prism
steps.instruction: Open a new project in GraphPad Prism, define the number of replicates, and paste the data in XY table format with replicates in adjacent columns.

steps.title: Plot mean fluorescence vs time
steps.instruction: Create an XY plot of mean fluorescence versus time; the software will display error bars automatically.

steps.title: Calculate fluorescence ratios
steps.instruction: In GraphPad Prism, select New Analysis → Results → ‘Remove baseline and column math’ to compute fluorescence ratios, normalizing as desired.

steps.title: Plot bar chart of ratios
steps.instruction: Copy the calculated ratios and standard deviations into a new table and generate a bar chart.

steps.title: Conduct two-way ANOVA on endpoint data
steps.instruction: Arrange endpoint fluorescence values with crRNAs in rows and samples/targets/concentrations in columns, then select New Analysis → Results → ‘two-way ANOVA (or mixed model)’ and add pair‑wise comparisons to display p‑values.

description: Collateral activity Type V and Type VI Clustered Regularly Interspaced Short Palindromic Repeats (CRISPR)-associated (Cas) proteins present promising opportunities for genetic testing by offering cost-effective, rapid, and point-of-care solutions.2,3,4 However, due to the mismatch tolerance exhibited by Cas proteins, achieving single-nucleotide fidelity in CRISPR-based diagnostics (CRISPRdx) is not inherently straightforward.1,5 Overcoming this challenge requires innovative approaches to enhance specificity, which have been the focus of numerous recent studies. This protocol outlines the steps to develop a CRISPR-based test for accurate detection of single-nucleotide variants (SNVs). A specific application that we validated involves high-fidelity detection of cancer-associated SNVs, trained on synthetic DNA, cell line-derived cell-free DNA (cfDNA), and evaluated on patient-derived plasma samples. However, this protocol can also be applied to multiple clinically relevant DNA sequences of interest, found in different types of samples, including other types of (liquid) biopsies (urine, tissue biopsy, etc.) or other cell lines than those described. This protocol focuses on optimizing Cas12a-based SNV detection by fluorescence, using PCR-based or isothermal amplification of DNA targets.
